column1: # Frame key|Route|Purpose and procedure|Important boundary

home|Home|Use Notes and Doc tabs to choose a workspace. Tap New note or New Doc to create there. The lower dock contains Library, voice capture, search and Filters. Open a card to continue writing; the content stays in private device storage.|A successful screen transition is not evidence that a pending external copy has finished. Read storage/save notices before disconnecting a folder.

notes-workspace|Home > Notes|Keep everyday writing and selected-text checklists together. Notes can contain mixed content without being silently turned into Docs. Tap the Notes tab to return from the Doc workspace, or swipe horizontally over the board when nothing is selected.|Existing older notes can use the earlier editor. Do not assume an editor change has reconstructed formatting that was never stored.

doc-workspace|Home > Doc|Use Doc for structured writing, tables, visual blocks and richer document composition. New Doc creates a separate document. Moving a note is different from making a Doc copy; review the action explanation before confirming.|A Doc is native MyNotes content, not a guarantee of Microsoft Word layout fidelity.

library|Home > Library|Library opens secondary destinations: Archive, Trash, Folders, Voice inbox, Settings, Open file and Viewed files. Checklist creation is available here in the Notes workspace. Tap a row to navigate; close the sheet to return without changing content.|This captured code41 frame still includes duplicate Notes/Doc rows. Candidate42 removes those rows; the Home workspace tabs remain.

filters-view|Home > Filters > View|Choose Grid view for compact cards or List view for one card per row. Options remain a draft until Apply filters. If a row is partly offscreen, scroll within the panel rather than tapping an unrelated underlying card.|View selection changes presentation, not stored note contents or folder placement.

filters-sort|Home > Filters > Sort|Choose last edited, created or title order. Apply to update the board. Candidate42 also adds arranged as per user after a Home drag, with persisted presentation IDs and pinned items still first.|The screenshot predates manual ordering. Drag ordering is a candidate feature awaiting Android qualification, not an accepted phone result.

filters-labels|Home > Filters > Labels|All notes means no label restriction. Otherwise choose any combination, optionally including Without a label. Select none deliberately produces an empty result. Use Manage labels to maintain names, then Apply filters.|Label filtering is any-of, not an all-labels intersection. Hidden notes are not deleted.

device-folders-filter|Home > Filters > Folders|Browse folders without treating labels as disk directories. Choose device folder opens Android's local folder selection. Library > Folders is another entry point into folder browsing.|A provider grant may be revoked or unavailable. Private content remains authoritative; do not clear app data to repair a missing external location.

search-keyboard|Home > search field|Enter a distinctive title, phrase or setting name. Search covers saved content and the bounded Viewed files index. Review each result category before opening: saved Notes/Docs, viewed originals and Settings are different destinations.|An empty result can reflect index limits or a changed file. Reopen the original to refresh its indexed text.

home-doc-swipe|Home > board gesture|Swipe horizontally across the board to switch between Notes and Doc when no cards are selected. Use tabs as the direct alternative. A vertical gesture scrolls cards instead of changing workspace.|A selected board uses selection actions; finish selection before workspace swiping. Respect reduced-motion settings.

editor|Home > note card|The title and writing area are editable. Use the upper Undo, Redo and Find controls and the contextual formatting/insertion tools. Keep the keyboard focused on the actual writing field and use Back to leave the editor.|An unsaved-looking toolbar does not mean original external TXT or Word files are being overwritten; imports are separate MyNotes copies.

editor-keyboard|Open a note > writing field|Tap writing to place the caret and type. Native selection handles support copying and selected-range operations. In short viewports some chrome adapts so writing remains reachable. Dismiss the keyboard when you need the full page tools.|Keyboard readiness and cursor position matter. Reopen the field if Android focus moved; avoid repeated taps that create duplicate notes.

adaptive-notes-rails|Note editor > landscape|Landscape redistributes tools into reachable rails while preserving the writing area between them. Rotate only after checking the current field and selection. Use the same action labels as portrait rather than hunting for a second command set.|Captured layouts are synthetic device profiles. Your font scale, keyboard and window size can produce different visible bounds.

adaptive-doc-rails|Doc editor > landscape|Structured Docs retain writing, Insert, Format and document actions in a narrower-height layout. Scroll the content instead of expecting every block to fit simultaneously. Return to portrait if an IME covers the intended control.|A landscape screenshot verifies one frame, not every orientation change or keyboard/vendor combination.

format|Note editor > Format|Select words to format that range, or place a caret for new typing. Bold, italic, underline and strike are inline choices. Clear removes applicable formatting without deleting the selected words. Check the scope indicator before applying.|Mixed selections can have partially active styles. A highlighted control is not a promise that every character shares one style.

adaptive-notes-format|Note editor > Format|The Format surface groups inline styles, font, size, paragraph style and numbering. Size steppers alter the chosen size within supported bounds. Reopen Format when you need another choice; keep text selection intact.|Formatting must not expand a selected range to the whole note unless the operation explicitly says so.

format-keyboard|Note editor > Format with keyboard|Open formatting while the writing field remains focused. The panel must stay reachable above or around the keyboard. Choose an option, then inspect the same selected text rather than assuming the cursor moved to the end.|If a control is clipped, scroll the panel or dismiss the keyboard. Do not save a different selection simply to bypass a UI defect.

stage-aa-selection|Doc > Format > selected text|A selected-range scope means the formatting applies to the chosen characters. Paragraph actions affect the paragraphs touched by that range. Check the preview and use Undo if the wrong scope changed.|Paragraph heading/numbering scope differs from character styling. Preserve the original selection while opening controls.

stage-aa-typing|Doc > Format > caret only|With an empty selection, an inline style can govern newly typed text. Existing earlier words stay unchanged. Enter a short sample, inspect the style and clear or toggle the pending choice before continuing plain text.|Moving the caret can inherit another run's style. Do not interpret every toolbar state as a document-wide setting.

document-format|Doc > Format|Use one formatting surface instead of unrelated Style submenus. Font, size, headings, numbering and clearing remain text operations; visual block tools belong to their own menus. Select the field inside a table or checklist when that is your target.|A table-cell selection is not the same as selecting the entire table block.

document-typing-style|Doc > Format > saved styles|A saved style stores formatting choices, not note text. Apply it to a selected range or compatible typing position. Choose meaningful names so a later document does not receive an unexpected font/size combination.|Saved styles are local settings. Portable note-only backups do not imply all profile settings were included.

document-saved-styles|Doc > saved styles|Review a stored style before applying it. Use the available management actions for obsolete entries. Undo the content change if a style was applied to the wrong range; managing a style and applying it are separate actions.|Restoring a note does not automatically restore every UI preference or saved-style profile.

numeric-h1|Writing > heading style|A paragraph heading changes visual hierarchy while retaining the actual numeric text. Select the intended paragraph and apply Heading1. Inspect glyph ascenders and descenders so large text is not mistaken for a clipped selection.|Heading size is not automatic outline numbering. Typed numbers remain authored characters unless a list operation transforms them.

numeric-h2|Writing > heading style|Use Heading2 for a subordinate section. Keep a consistent hierarchy within a long Doc and use Find to navigate distinctive headings. Clear returns selected text/paragraph formatting toward ordinary writing without erasing content.|Rendering can vary with Android fonts. Verify large text after rotation and re-opening, especially around line boundaries.

writing-lines|Editor > Appearance > Writing lines|Writing backgrounds guide your eye while you type. Choose the saved background you prefer and verify text remains legible. The guides are not underscore characters and should not change copying, search or text spans.|PDF printing may offer separate guide inclusion. A decorative background is not a guarantee of ruled paper in every export.

backgrounds|Editor > Appearance > backgrounds|Choose a background treatment independently from note colour. Inspect contrast with existing links, drawings and checklist boxes. Keep a neutral choice for dense content if decorative patterns compete with reading.|Background selection is presentation metadata; it must not flatten editable content into an image.

background-editor|Editor > saved background|The writing surface reflects the chosen background while native text remains editable. Scroll and type normally. Use Undo for content edits; use appearance choices when you only want a different visual treatment.|An appearance change should not be used as evidence that a pending content write completed.

palette|Editor > Appearance > colours|Select a note colour that keeps text, icons and links readable. Existing labels, images and diagrams remain in the same note. Inspect both light and dark appearance before relying on colour alone to communicate meaning.|Colour is not a substitute for a label or a descriptive title, especially for colour-vision accessibility.

word-appearance|Doc > Appearance|Use the document appearance panel for colour/background choices. Text formatting belongs to Format and image editing belongs to its object controls. Keep a consistent page treatment when composing a multi-section Doc.|This is native Doc appearance, not the Word original-file preview's authored page style.

note-find-sheet|Note editor > Find|Enter the exact phrase or a distinctive fragment. Review match counts and move through results. Find should keep writing context and not create a second duplicate search icon in the same toolbar.|Find does not change the text. A selection caused by Find still needs explicit editing or formatting to alter content.

note-find-result|Note editor > Find result|Inspect the highlighted match and adjacent text before replacing or typing. Move to the next occurrence when the same phrase appears in several paragraphs. Exit Find to return to ordinary writing.|Do not assume the first match is the intended replacement target.

find-keyboard-inline|Note editor > Find with keyboard|The inline query must remain usable with the keyboard visible. Keep the active field clear: typing in Find changes the query, while typing in the body changes content. Close Find before continuing prose.|Keyboard focus is not interchangeable with a visible selection. Check where new characters appear.

document-find-inline|Doc > Find|Search within structured document writing while keeping the surrounding Doc intact. Navigate each match and verify the correct text block or table-cell context. Close the search controls without rebuilding the document from extracted text.|Search navigation must not flatten images, drawings, tables or mixed blocks.

checklist|Notes > Library > Checklist|Create a list, write each item and tap a checkbox to change completion. Item controls provide indentation/reordering where available. The list title is distinct from item text. Keep completed items hidden only when you intentionally choose that view.|Hide checked is not delete. Existing item IDs, completion and indentation should survive saving and re-opening.

checklist-item-actions|Checklist > item options|Use the selected item's own control for operations such as indentation, movement or removal. Drag an item grip for row ordering; do not confuse the row grip with a whole-checklist block grip.|Actions must stay scoped to the selected item. Confirm the neighbouring items remain unchanged.

mixed-notes-selection|Note > selected text > convert to checklist|Select only the lines you want in a checklist, then use the conversion action. Unselected writing before and after stays ordinary text. Inspect checked states and formatting after conversion; use Undo for a single structural reversal.|Converting the whole note is a different operation. Do not accept a whole-document conversion as a selected-range fix.

stage-named-checklist|Doc > checklist box name|A named checklist groups related rows inside mixed writing. Tap the name or block grip for box-level options, including rename or movement. Give the box a descriptive name that is different from its first item.|The box name is persisted content. Unsupported older APKs may reject named blocks; do not downgrade important data.

stage-checklist-drop-preview|Doc > checklist block grip > drag|Drag the whole checklist toward the intended writing line and use the insertion marker before releasing. Holding near an edge can scroll. A tap-to-place movement alternative can be easier on a short screen.|Wrapped screen lines depend on font and width. The saved destination is a text position, not a permanent screen pixel.

content-item-drag|Doc > block move handle|Move one rich-content block using its grip and inspect the insertion marker. The block identity and contents travel together. Undo restores the previous structural placement rather than reconstructing a new block from a plain-text excerpt.|A cancelled or rejected drop must leave the original block where it was.

document-dragged|Doc > after block movement|Review the new ordering, surrounding writing and block-specific controls. Check tables, drawings and checklist rows remain editable. Re-open the document to verify the arrangement was saved.|Visual order alone does not prove that embedded rich content was preserved; inspect each moved object.

document-content-options|Doc > object overflow|Open the local options for the selected block instead of applying note-wide actions. Rename/copy/cut/paste and placement operations are scoped to the chosen content where supported. Read confirmation text before removal.|Clipboard object payloads and plain text have different fidelity. Do not promise unsupported external-app paste preserves native structure.

content-pen|Doc > content editing control|Enable the relevant editing mode before changing object content or block-scoped names. Keep a clear distinction between selecting a visual block and editing its internal text/cells. Return to ordinary writing when finished.|A grip should not open an unrelated Move item command merely because it was tapped.

content-list-caret|Writing > Insert > List at caret|With no selected words, insert a checklist/list at the caret using the available List action. Existing surrounding writing should remain. With selected words, inspect whether the action converts only that range.|Empty selection and nonempty selection have different semantics; check the result before adding more content.

content-typed-numbering|Writing > typed numbering|Typing a recognised numbering prefix can begin paragraph numbering. Continue with Enter when intended, and use Backspace/escape behaviour to return to ordinary writing on an empty numbered paragraph.|Numbering is structural formatting, not a reason to silently renumber arbitrary identifiers, phone numbers or pasted data.

mixed-note-header|Note containing rich blocks|A Notes-workspace item may contain selected-text checklist blocks and other rich content while remaining a Note. The header and toolbar should reflect the actual workspace, not assume every rich block means Doc.|Workspace membership is stored metadata, not reconstructed from a screenshot or a filename.

document-mixed|Doc > mixed content|Combine writing, checklists, tables, images, drawings and diagrams in a single native Doc. Use each object's local controls and preserve text between objects. Back should return through the document rather than an unrelated Settings page.|Exports may simplify some rich content. Keep a native backup when continued editing matters.

document-table|Doc > Insert > Table|Create a table, then edit a cell directly. Use the table's own overflow for structural actions instead of changing unrelated writing. Check row/column counts and header treatment before filling a large grid.|Table operations must retain other cells and surrounding blocks; a successful screenshot is not a complete data roundtrip test.

word-table-options|Doc > table options|Choose row/column changes and supported width/header options deliberately. Fit and fixed widths affect presentation. Inspect long cell text after a width change and confirm no cell contents disappeared.|Native Doc tables are separate from read-only Word-preview table fidelity, which remains limited.

doc-header-table|Doc > table header|Use a header row to identify columns and keep the body cells directly editable. Confirm header styling follows the saved setting rather than being inferred from the first row's text.|A visual header style does not automatically make a full Office spreadsheet or preserve every external table feature.

document-visuals|Doc > Insert > visual content|Add an image, drawing or diagram from Insert. Each type has its own editor and preview. Keep captions in editable writing rather than embedding all instructions into pixels.|Visual previews can be bounded for memory; the app must not claim the preview reconstructs lost original detail.

image-editor|Image > edit image|Review the image preview, then rotate, mirror or crop using the supported controls. Undo/Redo applies to the editing session. Save image edits only after inspecting the result; Cancel retains the prior note image.|Edits affect the saved MyNotes image copy, not the source file selected from the device.

image-crop-preview|Image editor > crop preview|Inspect the selected crop bounds before saving. A crop retains the selected pixels; it does not infer hidden detail outside the image. Reset or Undo if the boundary cuts off useful writing or a logo.|Keep a separate original when future uncropping or higher-resolution editing matters.

remove-image-confirmation|Image > Remove|Read the removal warning and cancel if the selected image is not the one intended. Removing a note image is distinct from editing its pixels or deleting the original external file.|A destructive-looking icon belongs to removal, not speech-engine opt-in or a harmless view change.

drawing|Editor > Insert > Drawing|Draw directly on the local canvas and inspect the stroke before saving. The drawing is inserted as a visual in the current note/Doc. Use the session controls rather than navigating away mid-stroke.|A preview is not a promise of infinite-resolution vector storage in every export.

drawing-tools|Drawing > tool controls|Choose the appropriate pen/eraser and supported colour/size controls. Test a short stroke before a large annotation. Zoom/pan should not be mistaken for ink input; keep the intended mode clear.|Undo an accidental stroke before saving. Canvas bounds and tool behaviour can differ from the surrounding text editor.

drawing-options|Drawing > options|Use available session actions deliberately. Clear canvas is destructive within the session and needs the proper confirmation; Cancel does not save a new drawing. Save returns to the note with the visual inserted.|Do not clear the whole note merely to start a new drawing.

diagram|Editor > Diagram|Add shapes, select one and drag its interior to move. Drag a selected corner to resize. Connect creates an arrow to another existing shape; diagram Undo/Redo handles structural changes.|The diagram uses a bounded logical canvas. Edges refer to stable shape IDs, not arbitrary screen positions.

shape-picker|Diagram > Add shape|Choose among the supported geometric shapes by name and preview. Place the new shape, then edit its label and colour. Geometric names help distinguish the visible form from legacy stored shape identifiers.|A shape's display name is not a conversion of its existing ID or text.

shape-dialog|Diagram > Edit shape|Select a shape first, then edit its text or colour. Save commits the change; Cancel keeps the existing shape. Inspect labels at the current size to avoid unreadable long text.|Editing one grouped member's label is different from moving or deleting the whole group.

diagram-options|Diagram > Diagram options|Group shapes and Edit arrows are available here. Candidate42 adds Split arrow, which inserts a small junction into a connector while retaining endpoints and label. Select the junction and Connect to branch.|The code41 screenshot does not show candidate42's new command. Native and phone checks are still required.

group-prerequisites|Diagram > Group shapes|Select at least two shapes to enable Group. Existing groups merge as units. Use Ungroup selected when the selected shape belongs to a group and you want separate movement again.|Grouping is not flattening: each shape and connector remains editable.

diagram-group|Diagram > grouped shapes|Dragging a member moves the group together with clamped geometry. Candidate42 long-press context offers Duplicate group or Delete group. Duplication copies internal arrows into an independent group, not external connections.|Deletion includes connected arrows and is undoable in diagram history. A duplicated group may overlap at canvas boundaries.

read-image-auto|Capture > Read from image|Choose a local image. Recognition runs on device with bundled English/Hindi/Kannada models and automatic language handling. Wait for review or Cancel reading. No language prompt is required for the default path.|OCR is fallible. Small text, blur, decorative fonts and emoji can be missed or misread, including emoji mistaken for Kannada digits.

image-text-selection|Read image > Select from image|The source image is visible behind text-region selection. Tap words, drag an area, use Choose words, or select all/clear. Pinch to zoom. Use selected text replaces the review text; saving the note is a separate step.|Keep selected image preserves pixels for emoji or objects the OCR cannot interpret. It is not universal emoji recognition.

ocr-review|Read image > review recognized text|Compare extracted text against the image, especially names, dates, digits, symbols and line breaks. Edit mistakes before Save as note or Append to note. Open Select from image again if you need a smaller region.|An engine confidence number is not calibrated correctness. Do not auto-convert real Kannada digits to emoji.

ocr-review-empty|Read image > empty review|If no text was detected, retain the original image and try a sharper crop or another source. You can type reviewed text manually. Saving actions remain unavailable until there is nonblank text.|Do not create an empty note as a substitute for an explicit OCR failure or missing-region explanation.

capture|Editor/Home > capture tools|Choose image reading, drawing or voice capture according to the content you need. Capture produces a reviewable local result rather than silently replacing existing writing. Check the current note target before inserting.|Mic permission is optional and should not be requested for unrelated text/image features.

doc-capture-language|Doc > image/voice capture|Capture results can append into the open Doc without flattening existing blocks. OCR language handling is automatic by default, while speech uses the selected offline engine. Review the result before insertion.|The fixture name is historical; it does not mean the current default OCR requires a language-selection prompt.

voice-inbox|Library > Voice inbox|Original recordings remain independently available for playback and transcript review. Code41 shows primary transport/progress with Recording options collapsed and the first20 cards loaded; Show more reaches the rest.|No recording is deleted by pagination. JSON note backups exclude original audio; export important recordings separately.

settings|Library > Settings|Settings groups appearance, speech, home-widget access, storage/recovery, diagnostics and About/offline models. Each descriptive card should explain its destination. Back should leave the current page rather than revisit an unrelated Settings route.|Experimental model labels are limitations disclosures, not proof of broad Indian-speaker accuracy.

settings-after-navigation|Secondary page > Back > Settings|Check the actual caller when using Back. Pages reached from Folders should return to Folders where appropriate, while ordinary Settings subpages return to Settings. Android Back and the visible Back action should agree.|Known route repairs do not certify every navigation sequence; report the exact entry path when a page returns incorrectly.

about|Settings > About & offline models|Read the version, privacy statement and bundled model/licence details. MyNotes has no account or Internet permission. OCR and speech run locally; other readers launched for originals control their own privacy/network behaviour.|The experimental Whisper adaptation uses one training speaker. Do not infer universal speech or emoji accuracy from its presence.

app-folder-copy-choices|Settings > Storage & recovery > App folder|Choose optional categories for a complete app recovery checkpoint in an empty selected App folder. Native content remains on device; selected copies provide additional recovery after reinstall and folder reselection.|Portable note-only JSON and complete app checkpoints have different exclusions. Read selected categories before assuming audio/settings/history are copied.

storage|Settings > Storage & recovery|Inspect the selected storage location, recovery options and backups. A private internal copy remains the content authority. Choose/reselect a local directory through Android, preserving grants and existing user files.|Do not uninstall, clear app data or downgrade while migration/recovery is unverified. Provider stalls do not mean private notes vanished.

folders|Library > Folders|Private folders and notes should become usable before optional connected-provider discovery completes. Open All notes or Main folder, select a subfolder or Create folder. Storage settings and Backups remain available.|This captured frame precedes restoration of the private-storage explanation/Backups card in candidate42. External checks can still wait behind provider work.

editor-folder-create|Editor > location > Create folder|Enter a valid folder name and confirm once. Wait for success before assuming the note has moved. Folder names and storage constraints are validated; a failed creation should leave note content intact.|Creating a folder and moving notes are distinct operations. Avoid repeated Create taps during an outstanding operation.

document-folder-sheet|Open document > Move to folder|Choose Main folder or a named destination, or create one from the sheet. Confirm the selected content target before moving. Closing the sheet without choosing must not relocate the document.|Connected-folder enumeration may still involve the storage provider. The first private-first browsing fix does not prove every move-sheet stall is removed.

backups|Settings > Storage & recovery > Backups|Export a readable native JSON note backup and keep a verified copy in local storage. Import first previews a merge; review conflicts and totals before Confirm merge. Important existing content gets a recovery snapshot.|JSON is not encrypted and excludes original recordings, settings and history unless a different complete-checkpoint feature explicitly includes them.

restore-preview|Backups > Import > preview merge|Compare the current library with the incoming snapshot. Review additions and conflicts, then Confirm merge only if the plan still matches the current library. Cancel before confirmation leaves notes unchanged.|A changed library invalidates the preview. Do not silently apply a stale plan or overwrite conflicting content.

trash|Library > Trash|Deleted notes remain recoverable for the retention period. Select an item and Restore to return it. Permanent deletion and Empty Trash are separate destructive operations with confirmation.|Original voice recordings have a separate lifecycle. A deleted transcript note does not automatically mean its audio was erased.

trash-confirmation|Trash > Delete permanently / Empty Trash|Read the warning, check how many items are affected and use Cancel if unsure. Permanent deletion is not ordinary Archive or Hide checked. Export important data before purging.|Do not promise Undo after a confirmed permanent purge. Seven-day retention is not a backup guarantee after app-data clearing.

labels|Editor/selection > Labels|Assign labels to organise content across folders. Use clear names and verify the intended note/selection receives them. Filters match any selected label. Rename and removal should not alter unrelated writing.|Labels are metadata, not device directories or a substitute for verified storage location.

add-reminder|Editor > reminder action|Choose a date/time only when you want a local reminder for that note. Inspect notification permission and battery constraints. Saved dates alone do not guarantee Android will display an alert.|Force-stop disables alarms until reopening; notification settings and battery policies can delay or prevent delivery.

reminder-date|Reminder > date picker|Select the intended future calendar date, then continue to time selection. Check month/year carefully around date boundaries. Cancel leaves the existing reminder unchanged.|A past date/time should be rejected rather than silently scheduling an unintended reminder.

reminder-time|Reminder > time picker|Choose the local time and confirm the complete future date/time. MyNotes uses the device's time and Android delivery system. Revisit the reminder if the timezone or travel schedule changes.|Local scheduling is not a cloud sync service and does not bypass Android notification/battery policies.

diagnostics|Settings > Diagnostics|Opt in only if you want app-event diagnostics. Export a report when investigating a failure; clear only with confirmation. Reports omit note bodies/audio/images/URI paths but environment details can identify a device.|Do not post private exports publicly. Event counts do not measure frame time or prove the physical cause of lag.

spreadsheet-grid-viewport|Library > Open file > CSV/XLSX|Open the local sheet as a read-only grid. Scroll rows/columns, choose a sheet where available and search cached values. CSV quoted multiline fields remain cell values; formulas are not executed.|Android CSV MIME aliases were repaired in code39. Current candidate bytes and provider combinations still require their own validation.

word-synthetic-paper-page|Open file > DOCX > MyNotes pages|The local paper preview renders supported inline images, text, explicit breaks and default headers/footers. Inspect the result against the authored original. Other views offers an installed compatible reader or a separate editable text copy.|This is approximate: substituted fonts, floating logos, merged tables, section rules, fields and legacy symbols may differ. No Word-equivalence claim.

word-zoom|Word/PDF preview > pinch|Pinch to zoom and drag to pan while zoomed. Double-tap resets/toggles the supported view scale. The lazy page raster remains bounded rather than allocating a giant bitmap for every pinch level.|Zoom changes the preview viewport, not the document's original page size or source bytes.

word-link-form|Doc > Insert > Hyperlink|Select the exact words, including multiple lines when intended, then enter a safe HTTP/HTTPS address. The selected words remain visible and styled as a link; the URL is separate from their display text.|Do not execute arbitrary URI schemes. Editing a link does not upload the note or replace the selected words with a guessed label.

document-pdf-options|Document actions > Export PDF|Choose the appropriate export options, including guide inclusion if offered. MyNotes writes a separate PDF and verifies the destination by readback. Keep the native document for continued rich editing.|A failed readback may leave a partial destination that needs removing. The native note and original external files should stay unchanged.

document-keyboard|Doc > writing with keyboard|Place the caret in the intended writing block before typing. Formatting, insertion and selection should preserve the active field across viewport adaptation. Scroll the document when the keyboard reduces space.|An accepted IME show request and actual active keyboard target are different states; inspect the current field if text goes elsewhere.
